findings.title: Task 2 breaks tsc -b in two test files it does not list
findings.claim: Task 2 changes `DuelTelemetry.players` from a tuple to `PlayerTelemetry[]`. Two test files index it with literal indices and no `!`. Under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` those become 'possibly undefined' errors, and `tests/**` is inside `tsc -b`. Neither file is in Task 2's Files list or its `git add`.
findings.evidence: plan L145-146 (Files), L500 (`players: PlayerTelemetry[]`), L604-605 (Step 12 tsc -b), L626 (commit list); tests/helpers/scriptedDuel.ts:78 (`t.players[0].repairsStarted`, `t.players[1]…` ×8 in telemetryLine); tests/duelTelemetry.test.ts:84 (`t.players[1].repairsStarted`); tsconfig.web.json:5 (noUncheckedIndexedAccess), :10 (include `tests/**/*`).
findings.why: Step 12's `npx tsc -b` fails. Step 12's fallback only covers `0 | 1` casts in src. An executor who fixes these files by hand leaves them out of the commit, so the Task 2 commit is red on tsc.
findings.fix: Add a Task 2 step: in tests/helpers/scriptedDuel.ts:78 write `t.players[0]!.` / `t.players[1]!.` (the telemetryLine text is unchanged, so gate output is untouched), and in tests/duelTelemetry.test.ts:84 write `t.players[1]!.repairsStarted`. Add both files to Task 2's Files list and its `git add`.

findings.title: Task 3 makes a crew-3 duel init valid, so duelMode.test.ts:134 fails
findings.claim: Task 3 widens `duelInitSchema.playerCount` to 2|3|4. On the Hound (4 spawns), `{ ...modeDuelInit(1), playerCount: 3 }` therefore validates and the duel mode's start returns ok. tests/duelMode.test.ts:134 asserts `.ok` is false. Task 3 Step 8 runs tests/duelMode.test.ts and expects PASS, but no task edits that line.
findings.evidence: plan L913 (`playerCount: z.union([2,3,4])`), L919-924 (only spawns/helm checks added), L965 (Step 8 runs tests/duelMode.test.ts), L986 (commit list lacks it); tests/duelMode.test.ts:26 (`modeDuelInit as duelInit`, the Hound), :134 (`encode({ ...duelInit(1), playerCount: 3 })).ok).toBe(false)`).
findings.why: The Task 3 commit leaves the suite red: Step 8's targeted run and Step 10's full run both fail.
findings.fix: In Task 3 change tests/duelMode.test.ts:134 to `playerCount: 5` (still refused). Optionally add `expect(duel.command({ kind: 'start', initBytes: encode({ ...duelInit(1), playerCount: 3 }) }).ok).toBe(true)`. Add the file to Task 3's Files list and `git add`.

findings.title: Task 7 removes otherStatus and ReadoutInput.other but misses four test files
findings.claim:
Task 7 deletes `DuelRuntime.otherStatus()` and `ReadoutInput.other`. Its sed and hand edits cover only crtReadout, duelConsoleModel, duelFireView, duelHealthView, duelReadout and duelOnlineView. Four other test files still use the removed API:
- tests/duelRuntime.test.ts and tests/scienceSeat.test.ts call `rt.otherStatus()`. That is a TypeError at runtime and a tsc error.
- tests/scienceConsole.test.ts and tests/scienceSeat.test.ts pass `other:` to `readoutRows`. That is an excess-property tsc error.
findings.evidence: plan L1647-1648 (Files and test updates), L1841 (sed file list), L1884 (`git grep otherStatus` must print nothing, but there is no step to fix the hits), L1894 (commit list); tests/duelRuntime.test.ts:79,107,120,175 (`rt.otherStatus()`); tests/scienceSeat.test.ts:88 (`rt.otherStatus()`), :68 (`readoutRows({ …, other: 'AT SCIENCE' })`); tests/scienceConsole.test.ts:84,86,87,90,101 (`other: 'WALKING'`/`'AT HELM'`); src/renderer/src/app/duel/runtime.ts:187,432 (the members Task 7 deletes).
findings.why: Task 7's targeted tests can pass while the full suite (Step 7) and `tsc -b` (Step 6) fail, so the commit is red. The executor has no stated replacement for these assertions.
findings.fix:
1. Add tests/scienceConsole.test.ts and tests/scienceSeat.test.ts to the sed command.
2. Rewrite the `otherStatus()` assertions with `crewStatus(rt.duel, 1)` (or the other pid): duelRuntime L79 and L120 'STANDING BY' become 'AWAY'; L107 and L175 'AT HELM' become 'HELM'; scienceSeat L88 'AT SCIENCE' becomes 'SCIENCE'. At L107 and L120, replace the array element.
3. List all three files in Task 7's Files and `git add`.

findings.title: Decision 5: REPAIRING shows for anyone standing near damage, even if not repairing
findings.claim:
The new rule is `repairInReach(d, pid) >= 0`. It is true for any conscious, standing, present character who is in a damaged or burning room within reach of its repair tile, whether or not they hold E. Two examples:
- In Single player, the idle partner left in a damaged room reads REPAIRING.
- Online, a crewmate walking past a damaged point reads REPAIRING.
Both old rules needed real work: the partner's held E, or repair progress since the last publication.
findings.evidence: plan L36 (Decision 5), L1776-1785 (`crewStatus`); src/renderer/src/app/duel/controls.ts:21-27 (repairInReach ignores input and progress); old rules at src/renderer/src/app/duel/runtime.ts:437 (`sentHeld[other].interactHeld && repairInReach`) and onlineSource.ts:151 (`workOf(d)[room] > prevRepair[room]`).
findings.why: The crew list is how Helm and Weapons know what the others are doing in the three-player playtest (the checklist asks about it). A false REPAIRING misleads them, and Task 7 deletes the tests that pinned the stricter behaviour.
findings.fix: Keep it state-only but require evidence of work: REPAIRING when `repairInReach(d, pid) = r >= 0` and the room has progress (`d.repair[r] > 0`, or the point's extinguish progress > 0 while it burns), else ON FOOT. Alternatively, keep the rule but label it `AT REPAIR`, and state this in Decision 5 and the checklist.
